title: The Great Story
label: The Great Story
line: The Bible as one story, from the first garden to the new city.
why: Every other hall assumes you know the story that formed the West. This is the way in, at the west door.

later.title: How the Bible came to be
later.question: Who wrote the Bible, when, and how should it be read?
voices: modern historical criticism and its critics, in our own words
later.note: Fills the gap against first-year university papers on the study of the Bible.

later.title: In the beginning
later.question: What does Genesis say about the world and us?
texts: Augustine, The Literal Meaning of Genesis (selections)
Darwin, as a voice in dialogue

later.title: The promise
later.question: Why does the story turn on one family?

later.title: Freedom and law
later.question: What is the law for?

later.title: Kings and prophets
later.question: What happens when a people asks for a king?
later.note: Mirrors a first-year paper on David.

later.title: Songs and wisdom
later.question: How do the Psalms, Proverbs and Ecclesiastes teach us to live?

later.title: The week that changed the world
later.question: What happened in the last week of Jesus's life?
texts: the Passion narratives in all four Gospels
voices: René Girard on the scapegoat, in our own words

later.title: The first Christians
later.question: How did a few followers of a crucified man change an empire?

later.title: The end of the story
later.question: Where is history going?

title: The Great Questions
label: The Great
Questions
line: God, reality and the hardest objections, faced honestly.
why: To be able to give a reason for what you believe, or don't, having heard the best case on every side.

later.title: What Christians believe
later.question: What does the Creed actually say, and why?
voices: modern doctrine in our own words

later.question: Why do people set places and times apart?

later.question: Why do the innocent suffer, and what does God owe us?

Gregory the Great, Moralia in Job
voices: C. G. Jung, Answer to Job (the objection)

later.title: Science and faith
later.question: Does science leave room for God?
texts: Galileo, Letter to the Grand Duchess Christina
voices: modern physicists and philosophers, in our own words

later.title: Miracles and history
later.question: Can a reasonable person believe in miracles?

Nicholas of Cusa, On the Peace of Faith

title: Know Thyself
label: Know
Thyself
line: The human person: desire, love, pride and the divided heart.

later.question: Why are we never satisfied?

texts: Stevenson, Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
Jung, Psychology of the Unconscious (Hinkle translation, 1916)

later.question: What are the kinds of love, and how do they go wrong?

label: The Noble
Life

later.question: What is courage, and where does it come from?

later.question: What do we owe each other?

later.title: Self-mastery
later.question: Can we govern ourselves?

later.question: How do we judge well in real life?

later.question: What are the virtues that look beyond us?

later.question: What are the sins that shape us without our noticing?

title: The Inner Life
label: The Inner
Life

why: At the east end of every cathedral is the altar. Everything else in the building points here.

later.question: Why did the saints go into the desert?
texts: Pascal on sitting quietly in a room

title: Athens, Rome and Jerusalem
label: Athens,
Rome and
Jerusalem
line: How we got here: the story of the West, told as a story.
why: From Homer to the modern world, the ideas we live by have a history. Knowing it makes you harder to fool.

later.question: What did the Greeks think a great life was?

later.question: Why did Athens kill its wisest man?

later.question: How do you stay free when you can't control your life?

later.question: What did Rome give the world?

voices: Roman law and the Justinian code, in our own words

later.title: The fall of Rome
later.question: What survives when a civilisation falls?

later.title: Monks who saved the West
later.question: How did monasteries carry learning through the dark centuries?

later.title: Reason and revelation
later.question: Can faith and reason agree?
voices: Maimonides, Avicenna and Averroes: how Aristotle came back to the West through Jewish and Islamic scholars

later.title: Cathedrals and universities
later.question: How did the medieval world build its institutions of learning?

Bernard of Chartres via John of Salisbury

later.question: What was the Reformation about, and what did it cost?

later.question: Did science and faith really go to war?

later.title: After the death of God: modern theology
later.question: How did Christian thinkers answer the twentieth century?

title: The City
label: The City
line: The common good: dignity, freedom, justice and the poor.
why: Faith was never only private. Our ideas of rights, care for the weak and the limits of power have deep roots.

later.title: Living not by lies
later.question: What does conscience owe to power?

Thomas Reid, Inquiry into the Human Mind
Adam Smith, The Theory of Moral Sentiments and The Wealth of Nations
Adam Ferguson, Essay on the History of Civil Society

later.title: The rule of law
later.question: Why should even kings be under the law?

later.title: Power
later.question: How should power be held?

texts: Tolstoy, The Kingdom of God Is Within You

later.title: The world church
later.question: What does Christianity look like beyond Europe?
texts: the Edinburgh World Missionary Conference of 1910
later.note: Fills the gap against university papers on world Christianity.

title: Beauty
label: Beauty
line: Art, music and poetry: where faith became colour, sound and words.
why: The West put its deepest beliefs into its art. Learning to see and hear it is learning a language.

later.title: How to read a painting
later.question: What are the old painters telling us?
texts: paintings from the National Gallery of Art

later.title: The English poets

later.title: Dostoevsky's wager
later.question: If there is no God, is everything permitted?
later.note: Replaces 'The great novels', with Tolstoy as its companion.

later.title: How should we live? Tolstoy
later.question: Can a great novelist find faith?
texts: Tolstoy, A Confession, The Death of Ivan Ilyich, Resurrection (Maude translations)

texts: George MacDonald, The Princess and the Goblin and 'The Fantastic Imagination'
